input.summary: Make the liability cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 and add standard uncapped carve-outs
input.comment: [Playbook] We have made the cap mutual and set it at the greater of the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim and USD 1,000,000, replacing the open-ended "fees paid for such Services" basis and the cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (which is the independent contractor clause, not an indemnity). Our position is that confidentiality, data protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP sit outside the cap, and that our payment obligations are not "damages"; if helpful, we can fall back to a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs at least for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

ops.oldText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY COMPANY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE CONSIDERED DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THE FOREGOING LIMITATION.
